Quirks at Work.text: For most people a Quirk is part of daily life, not a career: about four in five people have one, and nearly all of them work ordinary jobs in offices, shops, factories, farms, nursing and delivery. Public Quirk use is illegal without a license except in self-defense, so most people use theirs only at home or in small, harmless ways, and many workplaces forbid it on the clock. A Quirk that suits the work, a strong back on a loading dock or a cool touch in a kitchen, still comes up in job interviews. Part-time work is easy to find and hard to keep: convenience stores, restaurants, cram schools and event stalls are always short of help. Employers may ask about a registered Quirk where safety depends on it, and coworkers learn each other's powers through small talk, breakroom jokes and the occasional accident.
